newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices fall as speculators take profits.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices fall as speculators take profits.

text.p: Oil prices fell as the market came under pressure from speculators seeing the end of a recent bull run and predictions that U.S. stock data due later on Tuesday would show a long-awaited build in heating oil stocks ahead of the northern hemisphere winter.

The December contract for world benchmark Brent Blend crude from the North Sea fell 42 cents to $23.76 a barrel at 1601 GMT. "I think the trend has reversed in the short-term...It's looking toppy and a lot of people see a build in the heating oil stocks tomorrow," a broker said.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) is due to release weekly stock data, which brokers expect will show a build in both crude and heating oil inventories, which have so far been well below last year's levels.
Two big U.S. trading companies were the biggest sellers in the market, possibly taking speculative short positions ahead of a predicted build in heating oil stocks, brokers said.

Oil prices have rallied to a near six-month high in the last three months, partly because industry stocks were low ahead of the winter heating season. Iraq's continued absence from the market after a partial oil sales deal was scrapped by the United Nations also fed the rally.

Iraqi crude has been under a U.N. export ban since Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990. An oil-for-food plan under which Baghdad would be allowed to sell $2.0 billion in crude to buy food and medicine for a six-month period has been shelved indefinitely.

The United Nations postponed implementation of the May accord because Kurdish factional fighting in northern Iraq meant it could not guarantee the safety of monitors who would oversee food distribution.
Some analysts believe the plan could be implemented after the November 5 U.S. presidential elections.

"With the U.S. elections next week, the last major hurdle to the Iraqi humanitarian deal going through is removed. After next week you could hear more Iraqi crude oil talk again," said Charles Gray of Prudential Bache Securities.

A former Iraqi oil minister, Issam Chalabi, told an oil conference that at current oil prices, Iraq would export only 500,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude as opposed to the 700,000-800,000 bpd the market anticipated when prices were lower.
